text:
noah: Heads up — ops plan to rotate the KMS key used for EU GPU instance boot secrets next Tue 09:00 UTC. This is to meet compliance window but staging already showed a few provisioning failures after a key bump.

maria: @noah thanks. Do we have a rollback path? last time the firewall/NACLs blocking the KMS endpoint caused instances to hang on init. :eyes: 

kevin: I saw that in staging earlier today. Error looked like: 
```
2026-02-11T14:02:12Z boot-init ERROR: failed to retrieve secret from kms: AccessDeniedException
Caused by: network error -> TLS handshake timed out to kms.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com:443
```
Could be egress rules to the KMS endpoint or overly strict NAT gateway scaling.

noah: Good catch. We currently allow 0.0.0.0/0 outbound on the NAT for worker subnets, but firewall proxy is in front — proxy blocks calls signed with the new key prefix until we add the new key ARN to the allowlist.

aisha: Suggestion: don't rotate global key in one go. Plan: (1) create new key alias `alias/gpu-eu-rot-2026-02` (2) attach to a small canary pool (5% capacity) (3) validate boot and KV cache restore for bump, (4) roll forward if green, otherwise auto-revert.

maria: Also need to update the IAM condition on the KMS policy. Right now it checks `kms:EncryptionContext:deployment` to equal `gpu-eu-prod` which won't match new tooling until we update. We should update the policy to allow both aliases during transition.

kevin: I'll draft the firewall proxy change. Short-term we can add the new key ARN to the proxy allowlist and a specific egress rule to KMS endpoint. Long-term we want a service role that mints short-lived agent creds so no per-key allowlist.

noah: Ops-rotation-bot scheduled rotation job created: job id `rot-2026-02-16-eu-gpu`. It will run at Tue 09:00 UTC and call the canary set.

ops-rotation-bot: rotation job rot-2026-02-16-eu-gpu created by @noah. Monitoring hook: snyk-audit, kms-audit, and provisioning-trace enabled.

maria: From compliance: we must keep KMS audit logs in the central SIEM for 90 days. Make sure CloudTrail is sending `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:Decrypt`, `kms:GenerateDataKey*` events for the new key as soon as created.

kevin: Quick checklist I'm publishing here: 
- create new KMS key & alias (with key policy mirroring current)
- add key ARN to proxy allowlist
- add alias to IAM condition OR add alternate condition value
- create canary ASG (5% of eu-gpu capacity)
- patch autoscaler to route canary traffic
- run boot + KV restore test
- monitor tokens/costs for 24h
- roll remainder if green

aisha: For observability, add these trace points: provisioning attempt, kms fetch latency, kv-restore success, and fallback to cached prefix. If KV restore fails we should evict instance immediately to avoid sticky failures.

noah: Cost note — creating separate per-customer keys increases KMS monthly charges. Ops estimates +$1.8k/mo if we move to one-key-per-tenant for the EU fleet. Tradeoff: security isolation vs predictable capex. Thoughts?

maria: For enterprise customers with strict separation we should keep per-tenant keys behind a toggle. Default: shared regional key with strong key policy + audit. For locked accounts we offer dedicated key (chargeback).

kevin: Agreed. Also ops-savings: if we can use an internal signing proxy to mint short-lived data keys, we can reduce the number of KMS requests (GenerateDataKey) and cut cost. Need perf numbers first.

noah: Immediate action items: @kevin add key ARN to proxy allowlist and post PR, @maria update KMS policy draft & cloudtrail rule, @aisha set up the canary ASG and provisioning alert. We'll pause rotation if any of the canary boots fail.

kevin: PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/proxy/+/r1234 (adds allowlist entry and test harness). Please review.

maria: Policy draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/kms/eu-gpu-rotation.md — added alternate condition example and CloudTrail filter.

aisha: Canary ASG created. Provisioning test command: `./tools/provision-canary --pool eu-gpu --count 6 --kms-alias alias/gpu-eu-rot-2026-02` results posted to the canary monitor.

sre-bot: Canary run started at 2026-02-16T09:00:12Z. 6 instances requested, 6 instances launched, 4 succeeded, 2 failed with KMS AccessDenied. Investigating.

kevin: Failures look like the proxy didn't accept the new key ARN in 2 AZs due to replication delay in config push. Rolling back those two instances and requeueing.

noah: Pause rotation. Re-deploy proxy config with immediate propagation, rerun canary after 10m. We need to update runbook entry so on first fail we automatically roll the two failing AZs back to old key.

maria: Also open a CloudTrail log search: `eventSource:kms.amazonaws.com AND (errorCode:AccessDeniedException OR errorMessage:*AccessDenied*) AND eventTime>=2026-02-16T08:50:00Z` and link to incident.

aisha: Re-run canary at 2026-02-16T09:25 UTC. Monitoring shows 6/6 success. KV restore latencies: median 120ms, p95 380ms. No new errors.

noah: Great. Plan to proceed with staged rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m soak between steps and automatic pause on >1% failure rate or any AccessDenied.

maria: I'll update the compliance changelog and SIEM filters. After full rollout we need to validate audit logs landed and tag events with rotation job id.

kevin: I'll follow up with a proposal to remove per-key allowlist from the proxy and instead validate signatures in the proxy by role. That will simplify future rotations.

noah: Thanks all. Triage notes + runbook edits in the rotation ticket: https://tickets.redwood.ai/ROT-8762. Closing this thread for day — ping here if anything breaks during rollout. :lock:
